
# SQLiLite

![PicoCtf/SQLiLite 20261015-171850.png](data:image/png;base64,)

This was a challenge Testing Basic SQL injection vulnerabilities which was tagged as __MEDIUM__
Despite that I found it easier I even suppose it was overtagged so yeah so lets get at it
First I launched the instance which landed on to a login page :

![PicoCtf/SQLiLite 20261015-172227.png](data:image/png;base64,)

From the login page I first tried to inspect the html but I knew I will not get anything.Without wasting time I injected the generic SQL payload any attacker would inject on `' or '1'='1` 
However simpler this payload looks it does its magic every time,so I filled in the username with `Admin` to get the highest privileges in case I would want to navigate to any endpoint on the page

![PicoCtf/SQLiLite 20261015-173211.png](data:image/png;base64,)

After the successful login I knew the flag was near so I tried to test different endpoints on the URL but none had the flag then I just decided to do what any rookie would do in this situation
Inspect this page!!
There it was on plain sight:

![PicoCtf/SQLiLite 20261015-173554.png](data:image/png;base64,)
